reader.requirement: At 1985 every literal in SUBTRACT (literal-1 before FROM in formats 1 and 2, literal-2 after FROM in format 2) must be a numeric literal; the only figurative permitted is ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES, with ALL redundant at 1985 (IV.4.2.2.2.3), so nonnumeric literals, SPACE, HIGH-/LOW-VALUE, QUOTE, ALL literal and symbolic-characters must be refused and ZERO (with or without ALL) and signed/decimal/18-digit numeric literals accepted.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.Check(FigurativeAllZeroNumericRemoved2002): ALL ZERO as an arithmetic operand accepted at 85, COBOL0902 from 2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: SUBTRACT ALL ZERO FROM N compiles and runs at --std 85 (10=[+0013]) and is COBOL0902 at --std 2023; every other literal form behaves the same at both
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover a nonnumeric literal-1 and literal-2; figuratives (SPACE, HIGH/LOW-VALUE, QUOTE, ALL literal, symbolic-character, ZERO and ALL ZERO) are not exercised

probes.printed: COBOL0844 on all 11 statements: "1" (formats 1 and 2, both positions), SPACE, HIGH-VALUE, QUOTE, ALL "1", LOW-VALUE as literal-2, symbolic STAR, ALL "5" as literal-2

probes.expected: ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES, ALL ZERO, negative, decimal and 18-digit literals legal; size error leaves N unchanged

probes.printed: --std 2023: COBOL0902 at line 32 (ALL ZERO as an arithmetic operand removed in COBOL-2002)
probes.expected: the 1985 arm accepts ALL ZERO; later editions refuse it

reader.notes: The one numeric-context reader refuses every non-numeric literal and figurative but ZERO; the ALL ZERO edge is edition-gated and the 1985 arm accepts it, as the 1985 text's redundant-ALL rule requires. Minor wording point: the 1985 COBOL0844 text for SPACE etc. says ZERO is permitted 'WITHOUT the ALL phrase', which is the 2002+ rule; the refusal itself is right.
